name: opencode
notes: On 2.2.2 with deepseek/deepseek-flash: one read-only turn read a file and had no edit or shell tool; one native-write turn edited a file and had no shell tool; one resume kept the session. A later native-write turn edited a file inside the run directory, while reading or writing outside it by absolute or ../ path was refused with external_directory. The skill tool is listed, but loading an installed skill is refused with "Permission denied: skill". --standalone loads the inline permission policy in a private local process; without it the background service ignores OPENCODE_CONFIG_CONTENT. OpenCode takes its project directory from PWD, which the runner sets to the run directory. Managed configuration outranks the inline policy (https://opencode.ai/docs/config/#precedence-order), so managed paths cause refusal before CLI invocation. The MDM guard includes /Library/Managed Preferences to cover both global and per-user ai.opencode.managed.plist files, conservatively refusing even unrelated managed preferences; the macOS and Linux guards were not run on those systems. read-only retains the deny-by-default reading policy. native-write adds edit only: file edits without shell; OpenCode's external_directory permission, not an OS sandbox, keeps them inside the run directory; bash, webfetch, task, and other unlisted tools remain denied. Effort variants use #variant in the model ID; this adapter does not support an effort option. --title avoids an extra model call to name the session.
